ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A particle starts from the origin of an x-y Cartesian coordinate system, moving 6 m in the positive $\mathbf{X}$ direction in the first 1 s, and 8 m in the positive y direction in the second 1 s.

1. Determine the magnitude and direction of the displacement of the particle during these 2 s.
2. Determine the magnitude of the average velocity of the particle during these 2 s.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
10m, at an angle of 53^{\circ} with the positive direction of the x-axis
5m/s

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A particle starts from the origin of an x-y Cartesian coordinate system, moving 6 m in the positive x direction in the first 1 s, and 8 m in the positive y direction in the second 1 s. 1. Determine the magnitude and direction of the displacement of the particle during these 2 s. 2. Determine the magnitude of the average velocity of the particle during these 2 s.
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: 10 m, at an angle of 53^{\circ} with the positive x-axis 5 m/s
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The motion consists of two perpendicular displacement components: 6 m along the positive x direction during the first second, then 8 m along the positive y direction during the second second. Thus the net displacement vector is Δr = (6 m)i + (8 m)j. Its magnitude is |Δr| = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(36 + 64) = sqrt(100) = 10 m. The direction relative to the positive x-axis is given by tanθ = 8/6, so θ = arctan(8/6) ≈ 53°. The total time is 2 s, so the magnitude of the average velocity is |v_avg| = |Δr|/Δt = 10 m / 2 s = 5 m/s.
